title: Split Synchronization Orchestra Protocol (WIP)
content:
Context and goal:

This is a working playbook for coordinating split-assignments across multiple services (frontend router, auth proxy, reranker, personalization service, and Redwood routing) when we run progressive exposure experiments. The key risk we've observed: independent feature flags or routing rules drifting out-of-sync between services, producing inconsistent user experiences and noisy signals. This doc proposes an "orchestra" protocol to keep splits synchronized, ensure telemetry alignment, and automate safe fallback.

Intended audience:
- Product release leads
- Release engineers / infra oncall
- Observability & SRE reps
- Solutions engineers owning customer rollouts

When to use:
- Multi-service feature launches that require traffic partitioning (A/B, multi-variant, hybrid inference routing)
- Canary waves that span more than one service boundary
- Rollouts with cross-team slos (latency/cost/quality) that need deterministic slicing

Core principles:
1) Single source of truth: one canonical split manifest published to Redwood Console (or a central key-value) and consumed by downstream routers.
2) Deterministic mapping: the same split key must yield the same assignment across all services (hashing + salt).
3) Observable handshake: every activation must emit a split-bound event (trace/span) so we can correlate downstream traces to upstream assignment.
4) Fast reversible changes: any exposure increase must have an automatic short-circuit circuit-breaker (time + degradation rule).
5) Human-in-the-loop checks for early waves; automation for later waves.

Protocol (orchestra) overview — high level steps:
1) Draft split manifest (json): variant ids, percentages, salt, rollout id, start_time, owner, abort_criteria.
2) Publish manifest to Console API and tag in GitHub (PR references).
3) Run small synthetic-sanity run (0.1% traffic) with synthetic headers to validate routing path across services.
4) Run wave 0 (human-only): route small internal cohort (employees + canary orgs). Observe primary signals for 24–48 hrs.
5) Waveed increases: automated schedule with condition gates (latency, error-rate, quality-signal).
6) Final cutover: once guardrails pass for N cycles, flip routing default to new variant and retire manifest.

Concrete manifest example (schematic) — publish as single-line JSON in Console:
{"rollout_id": "R-2025-01-ml-34", "variants": [{"id":"v1","pct":70},{"id":"v2","pct":30}], "salt":"s-e9f4", "owner":"maya@redwood.ai", "abort_on": ["latency_p90>600ms","quality_regression>3%"], "trace_key":"split_assignment"}

Sync handshake checklist (pre-publish):
- [ ] Hash function and salt agreed in spec (sha256 modulo 10000)
- [ ] Console manifest validated by router and SDK unit-tests
- [ ] Integration test that asserts identical assignment for 100k synthetic keys across services
- [ ] Observability spans instrumented: upstream assignment, downstream decision, fallback events
- [ ] Jira ticket created with rollback owner and SLAs

Monitoring signals (priority order):
1) Functional correctness: mismatch rate between upstream assignment event and downstream observed variant tag (>0.1% triggers investigation)
2) Latency: 95th and 99th percentile by variant and route
3) Error budget: errors per variant (5xx, timeouts) relative to baseline
4) Quality metrics: rerank NDCG lift, hallucination proxy, user edit rate (product specific)
5) Cost: token-rate and GPU utilization per variant

Automated gating example (pseudocode):
- Increase from 1% -> 5% if last_4h(latency_p95_delta) < 30ms AND last_4h(errors_rate_delta) < 0.2% AND last_4h(quality_regression) < 1%
- Otherwise pause and notify owners

Rollback & escape hatch patterns:
- Immediate rollback: set manifest to 0% for target variant via Console API (curl example below).
- Fallback layering: if downstream service fails to read manifest, default deterministic assignment to control variant. Never default to new variant.
- Circuit-breaker: platform will automatically reduce exposure by 50% if latency_p95_exceeds threshold for more than 5 minutes.

Sample Console API commands (dev-only endpoints):
- Publish manifest:
  curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/splits" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @manifest.json
- Quick set to zero (emergency):
  curl -X PATCH "https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/splits/R-2025-01-ml-34" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"variants":[{"id":"v2","pct":0}]}'

Roles & ceremony:
- Conductor (release lead) — coordinates publish, approval, and escalation
- Router owner(s) — validate integration and run synthetic checks
- Observability lead — pre-wires dashboards, alert rules, golden queries
- SRE oncall — monitors infra signals and executes emergency rollback
- Product owner — approves business metrics and quality gates

Operational runbook (quick):
1) If mismatch_rate > 0.1%: pause rollout, open incident, assign router owner to debug mapping logic.
2) If latency_p95_delta > threshold: reduce exposure by 50% and notify SRE.
3) If quality_regression >= abort threshold: immediate 0% rollback and postmortem.

Open questions / things to decide:
- Ownership of the canonical manifest: Console or a separate config service? (tradeoffs in latency and auditability)
- Slicing keys: should we use user_id, device_id, or hashed session_id for split determinism across mobile and web?
- How to model multi-variant ramp arithmetic to avoid rounding drift across microservices?
- Standardized quality metrics for LLM features (schema + sampling cadence).

Next actions (short term):
- [ ] Prototype a single-source manifest read endpoint and add SDK integration tests (assigned: Javier)
- [ ] Create synthetic-sanity harness for cross-service assignment parity (assigned: Priya)
- [ ] Draft standardized split event spec (trace/span fields) and ship to trace schema (assigned: Samir)

Notes and references:
- See linked Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-PLATFORM-4532) for prior experiments and telemetry schema.
- Related Jira (RNO-1189) tracks early production mismatches encountered during the reranker rollout in Nov 2024.

Notes-to-self (quick): keep waves small and avoid concurrent unrelated rollouts that re-use the same split key. If multiple rollouts must coexist, require explicit mutual-exclusion or namespace the salt.
